steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Lord's Prayer (Matthew 6:9-13) is the most important Christian prayer. Jesus taught it to his disciples when they asked him how to pray. It includes praise ("Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name"), petition ("Give us today our daily bread") and confession ("Forgive us our debts").

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — Prayer
steps.body: 1. For Prayer questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Prayer to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
